value.overview: The Whiskered Screech-Owl (Megascops trichopsis) is a owl recorded in the United States. Field recognition often comes from small owl size, ear tufts, yellow eyes, dark streaking, and a whistled or trilled voice in oak-pine canyon habitat. In the U.S. source data, it appeared in 2 state or DC summaries, including AZ, NM. It is most associated with Forests:  Mesoamerican Pine-Oak, and local season should be checked before trip planning.

value.identification: Look for small owl size, ear tufts, yellow eyes, dark streaking, and a whistled or trilled voice in oak-pine canyon habitat. Also use size, posture, flight style, voice, behavior, habitat, and season. Plumage can vary by sex, age, molt, and light, so the safest identification comes from combining several field marks rather than relying on one color or feature.
